n: In that day Judah will sing a new song: “We have a strong city, and God makes salvation its walls and ramparts.” Zion’s security is God Himself, not stone walls.
Open the gates so that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter. This resembles ancient temple-entrance songs.
A beloved promise: God will keep in perfect peace the person whose mind is fixed on Him, because that person trusts Him.

f.g: Hebrew shalom shalom — peace doubled, complete peace.

f.w: whose mind is stayed on thee

n: Trust the Lord forever, because Jehovah is an everlasting Rock.

f.g: Hebrew Yah YHWH — a doubled form of God’s name for emphasis.

n: He humbles those who live in lofty pride and levels the proud city to the dust.
The poor and needy, once trampled, will now walk over the ruins of their oppressors. God reverses fortunes.
The path of the righteous is level; God, the Upright One, makes it smooth.
Walking in the way of God’s judgments, we wait for Him. Our deepest desire is His name and remembering Him.
Isaiah longs for God through the night and seeks Him early. When God’s judgments are on the earth, people learn righteousness.

f.w: when thy judgments are in the earth

n: Even when shown kindness, the wicked won’t learn righteousness. In a land of goodness they still do wrong and never see God’s majesty.

f.w: Let favour be shewed to the wicked

n: Lord, Your hand is raised, but they don’t see it. They will see Your zeal for Your people and be ashamed, and the fire reserved for Your enemies will consume them.

f.g: Better “zeal for the people” — God’s passion for His own.

n: Lord, You give us peace; everything we have achieved, You have done for us.

f.w: thou also hast wrought all our works in us

n: Other masters have ruled over us — foreign kings and false gods — but we honor Your name alone.
Those tyrants are dead and will not rise again. God has wiped out even the memory of them.

f.g: The oppressors have no future; contrast verse 19.

n: Lord, You have enlarged the nation and extended its borders; You have won glory.
In distress they sought You, Lord, whispering prayers when You disciplined them.
Like a woman in hard labor crying out in pain, so were we before You, Lord.

f.w: Like as a woman with child

n: We labored and writhed but gave birth only to wind. We could not bring salvation to the earth by our own efforts. Only God can save.

f.w: we have not wrought any deliverance

n: A glorious promise of resurrection: “Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!” As dew revives plants, God will bring the dead out of the earth.

f.w: together with my dead body shall they arise

f.g: Dew of light — life-giving morning dew.

n: Come, my people, go into your rooms and shut the doors; hide for a little while until God’s wrath has passed — like Israel sheltering at the first Passover.
For the Lord is coming out of His dwelling to punish the earth’s people for their sins. The earth will expose the blood shed on it and no longer hide its slain. Hidden crimes will be revealed.

f.w: the LORD cometh out of his place
